title: Implement exact FFT word multiplication on fixed tapes
body:
I implement exact unsigned n-bit multiplication in the retained fixed-tape model, with `O(n log2(n+2)^2)` time and `O(n)` space. I apply the classical radix-digit reduction through corrected [PR3709](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3709), head `62264289adb01f3ba4930cd0154c75887f96203c`, while retaining its internal Karatsuba multiplier. The dependency is acyclic.

I choose `b=ceil(log2 n)`, `q=ceil(n/b)`, minimal `r=2^ell>=2q`, and `p0=2b+ell`. The normalized return `Q_p0(fg/r)` has exact ordinary convolution coefficients as real numerators because `2^p0=r*2^(2b)` and the degree is below r. Sequential carries recover the exact 2n-bit result. I preserve borrowed values and heads, consume protected child outputs and restore fixed scratch. The full bill includes unamortized twiddle setup for A=C=1.

This supplies a concrete scalar primitive for the Gaussian arithmetic handoff after [PR3763](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3763). With delta=.0001, I derive arithmetic power .9981 below the inherited full Fourier power .99827619697. I leave Gaussian coefficient production, guarded convolutions, factor-page access, window restoration and the complete CRT/integer join open.

I started from canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6, and recorded the expansion decision before implementation in [Discussion3664](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664). Before submission I refreshed main and searched 491 open PRs and 2,509 Discussion records. The PR changes only `research/physical-fft-word/`.

I register seven suites: actual default FFT products at 17 and 19 bits, integration with the retained signed Arithmetic caller, base reuse, separate codec fixtures through 1,024 bits, large encoded geometry, 13 failure controls, source authentication and exact cost arithmetic. `PROOF.md` gives the all-size argument; `EVIDENCE.md` distinguishes full execution from codec and metadata checks. Reproduce with `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/physical-fft-word`.

Validation at `9b5474f47b0ea9a3c76bb5b1b577fb36704815e0`:

- I passed all seven registered suites locally, plus metadata, committed-byte and source-history checks.
- I replayed the official committed export outside Git on Darwin arm64, Python 3.12.13, and checked that all 22 regular files, including the receipt, stayed unchanged. The full FFT sequence took 152.451 seconds and returned the same exact products.
- Export SHA256: `d428e8b6aef4d348fa2e922ca64c4cfd634bbb2f0c150033273e65fcf4600b49`; receipt SHA256: `237ccd34aadda692f73b85277816b76168acaecfe06a12996cce37a7f0925cbc`.
- I verified all seven hosted suites and the unchanged-input check in [CI39166027769](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39166027769), which completed with success at this head. I matched its tested merge tree to the publication tree `97bbd90bca3ae03b8b6d9e6044b1fd5f3a2d2be0`.

I retain PR3709's numerical precision/recovery premises and [Arham Tahir's separate audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664#discussioncomment-19022515) as pending author work. I credit the standard FFT/radix and Karatsuba algorithms, Mason Hale's certified interval reference, Dugongue's scalar-ABI precedent, the retained rad20 Gaussian reports and the nested source notices. I leave the selected frontier unchanged. Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation, source analysis and checks; I claim no independent human or formal-kernel review.
